title: Grill round 3 — where stacks live in Settings
summary:
Your round-2 note: *"Should we keep a Stack option/page in Settings, or combine this with the Harnesses page? What's the better UX UI we can have here?"*

My take: **merge them**. Almost everything this round adds is a property of an *account* — its quota meter, its cooldown and Clear button, its login/install status, why it was skipped — and every "fix it" hint (banner, blocked card) already points at **Harnesses**. With a separate Stacks page, the user reads the problem on one page and fixes it on the other. A stack is a group of accounts, so it reads best as a group on the accounts page.

proven.text: Settings sections today: General, Harnesses, Stacks, Agents, Pipelines, Git, Prompts. The Stacks editor is already a sub-page (`stack-editor` view) with its own dirty-state guard, so it can be reached from anywhere.

proven: The "no usable account" banner currently says "fix one in Settings → Stacks", but every cause it can name (disabled, logged out, not installed, model, CLI version) is fixed on the Harnesses page.

questions.title: Where should stacks live in Settings?
questions.why: Decides which page gets the new per-account quota, cooldown and history UI, and how the two e2e settings specs are rewritten.

options.label: Merge into Harnesses: stacks render as groups of their accounts
options.description: Harnesses shows each stack as a card holding its accounts in order (primary first), each a full account row with status, quota meter, cooldown + Clear. Accounts in no stack are listed below. The card header has the stack actions: Edit (opens the existing editor sub-page: order, members, mirror mode, preview, Restore), History, Delete. "New stack" sits at the top. The Stacks sidebar entry is removed; old deep links open Harnesses.
options.consequence: One page to read and fix; the Stacks section and its list view go away; both settings e2e specs are reworked.

options.label: Keep a separate Stacks page, cross-linked
options.description: Stacks stays its own section with quota, cooldown, history; each account row links to its Harnesses row, and Harnesses rows show a stack chip linking back.
options.consequence: Smaller UI change; account state is shown in two places.

options.label: One page with two tabs: Accounts | Stacks
options.description: Same data as today's two sections under one sidebar entry.
options.consequence: Still two views of the same accounts; mostly a navigation change.

recommendation.reason: The account is the unit you read and fix; grouping by stack shows order and state in one place and removes the page hop.
